bull_bear.body:
- Board approved a maiden interim dividend of ₹8/share.
- Deleveraging: Net Debt/EBITDA improved to 0.9x (footnoted TTM) from 1.3x in Q4FY26, with net debt down ₹3,481 Cr to ₹29,532 Cr from ₹33,013 Cr; the deck attributes this to being 'In line with Strong Profitability'.
- Credit rating upgraded to AA+ (Stable) by both ICRA and CRISIL.
- Balance sheet: cash and cash equivalents of ₹6,068 crore; total consolidated debt $3.8 bn / ₹35.6K Cr (term debt $3.5 bn / ₹33.3K Cr plus WC/short-term borrowing $0.2 bn / ₹2.3K Cr) versus $4.0 bn / ₹37.7K Cr in Q4FY26; debt mix 89% INR and 11% USD/foreign currency, unchanged QoQ.
- Debt management: average term debt maturity at ~3.5 years described as 'Proactive credit management', with interest expense of ~8.9% (Q1 FY27 average); long-term maturities laid out as 5.9 / 6.0 / 4.1 / 5.1 / 12.3 ('000 ₹ Cr) for FY27 / FY28 / FY29 / FY30 / FY31 & Beyond.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- Describes itself as India's largest aluminium producer and 'one of the world's leading producers of aluminium', operating integrated, world-class assets including a state-of-the-art alumina refinery, 'one of the world's largest aluminium smelter complex in Odisha', and BALCO (Bharat Aluminium Company).
- Serves customers across more than 60 countries and states it 'plays a vital role in global industrial supply chains'.
- States the Lanjigarh refinery is 'Placed among the Top 3 Alumina refineries globally', and that Q1FY27 alumina purity of 98.81% was a best-ever.
- Management frames strategy around 'resource security, operational integration, and value-added products', with the company 'building one of the world's most competitive, fully integrated aluminium businesses' and continuing to 'strengthen raw material security'.
- CFO frames demand pull from 'energy transition, infrastructure, transportation, packaging, and advanced manufacturing sectors across India and global markets'.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Demerger] This is the company's first quarter as an independent listed entity (BSE: 544780, NSE: VAML). The deck notes 'While Vedanta's demerger became effective from May 1, 2026, the figures reported here are for the full quarter (April-June'26).'
- [Sensitivity] Stated sensitivities: a ₹1 depreciation in USD/INR increases EBITDA by ~₹675-725 crore/year; a 100 $/t movement in LME aluminium impacts EBITDA by ~₹2,000 crore/year (against a Q1FY27 LME of 3,571 $/t).
- [Governance/Compliance] Deck reports 99.73% compliance status in Q1 and 17.12% of Category-A NCs closed in Q1 (the deck's layout leaves these two figures' pairing to their labels ambiguous — see notes).
- [Ash logistics] Ash utilization is to improve 'through diversified off-take channels, mine backfilling, enhanced rail evacuation (>50%), and 45 days of additional ash storage capacity'; dyke space stated as 45 days VAML-J, 140 BALCO, 200 VAML-L.
business.title: Notable from the deck

deepdive.thesis: The deck positions Vedanta Aluminium Metal Limited as India's largest aluminium producer and one of the world's leading producers of 'the Metal of the Future', building one of the world's most competitive, fully integrated aluminium businesses on the back of raw-material security, cost leadership and a widening value-added portfolio in its first quarter as an independent listed entity.
